summary:
Región del Bío-Bío stands under Chile's national framework for trans people; the findings below are those specific to the region.

Movilh's XXIII annual human rights report, covering 2024 data and published in March 2025, attributes 5.89% of Chile's documented cases of discrimination and violence on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity to Bío-Bío, the third-highest share of any region. Concepción is listed among the cities recording the most documented incidents, with five. That figure is a raw count: the report ranks cities by number of documented cases, which tracks population size, and it publishes no per-capita rate for the region.

Regional health services have been the subject of formal complaints. In October 2016 Movilh-Biobío filed a complaint with the Seremi de Salud, naming Mauricio Careaga Lemus, over the treatment of patient Hanna Jiménez Carrasco at the Hospital Traumatológico de Concepción. Jiménez Carrasco was interned from 28 September to 3 October 2016 and was placed and treated as male, despite the legal duty to use a trans patient's chosen name and social sex. The complaint described the staff conduct as brutal and illegal discriminatory acts.
tangentialFactors:
The regional figures come from a national report's breakdown by region, so Bío-Bío's 5.89% share is measured against the national case total rather than against the region's own population; no regional per-capita rate is published.

The 2016 hospital complaint was filed before the 2018 extension of the anti-discrimination law to gender expression and before the gender identity law took effect in December 2019; the duty to use a patient's chosen name and social sex that the complaint invoked rested on the health policy in force at the time.
localsOnly:
For residents, the documented route for challenging discriminatory treatment in a regional health facility is a complaint to the Seremi de Salud, the regional health authority; Movilh-Biobío is the organisation that filed the 2016 complaint over the Hospital Traumatológico de Concepción.

The 2024 case data concerns incidents documented in the region, including in Concepción, and reflects the volume of complaints and reports reaching a national advocacy organisation rather than a count of all incidents occurring in Bío-Bío.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not record the outcome of the 2016 complaint to the Seremi de Salud, whether the hospital was sanctioned, or whether the practice changed.

No region-specific figures on anti-trans violence, hate-crime prosecutions, or enforcement of the national hate-crime aggravating circumstance in Bío-Bío were identified.

No region-specific rules on facilities access, document processing at regional Civil Registry offices, or regional health-care policy for trans patients were identified beyond the 2016 complaint.
